correctness.rationale: The positive Dirichlet Laplacian has an explicitly reconstructible Green diagonal \(G_m(t)=(1-r^{2m})/\sqrt{t(t+4)}\), with \(t=(1-r)^2/r\). The resolvent Cauchy–Schwarz bound yields \(K_m\le\sup_t2\sqrt t G_m(t)\); at the unique maximum of this function, differentiating \(G_m\) gives \(\|Dg_t\|_2^2=t\|g_t\|_2^2\), so the upper bound is attained and equality vectors are exactly multiples of \(g_t\). The logarithmic derivative is a product of strictly decreasing positive terms, giving unique \(r_m\) and strict site monotonicity. With \(a_m=-m\log r_m\), the critical equation is \(e^{2a_m}-1=4m\coth(a_m/(2m))\); it gives \(a_m=\log m-\frac12\log\log m+\frac12\log8+o(1)\). Expanding \(K_m=(1-e^{-2a_m})\operatorname{sech}(a_m/(2m))\) yields the stated logarithmic deficit. The actual check_halfline.py uses monotone root finding, finite extremizers and random checks; its code was inspected, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Optimal interpolation constants at specified distances from a Dirichlet boundary and their distinct logarithmic approach to the whole-lattice constant are natural analytic invariants. The complete equality cases and sharp leading/three-term deficit are useful boundary-layer information not supplied by the general resolvent method alone.

final_claim: For Dirichlet half-line sequences \(u_0=0\), the optimal interpolation constant at site \(m\ge1\) in \(\lvert u_m\rvert^2\le K_m\|u\|_2\|Du\|_2\) is \(K_m=\frac{2\sqrt{r_m}}{1+r_m}(1-r_m^{2m})\), where \(r_m\) is the unique root in \((0,1)\) of \((1-r)(1-r^{2m})=4mr^{2m}(1+r)\). All extremizers are scalar multiples of the Dirichlet resolvent vector. The constants increase strictly from \(K_1=4/(3\sqrt3)\) to 1 and \(8m^2(1-K_m)=(\log m)^2-(\log m)\log\log m+(1+\log8)\log m+o(\log m)\).
limitations: The inequality is for real square-summable sequences on the homogeneous discrete half-line with a Dirichlet endpoint, not a continuum Sobolev theorem.
The numerical script checks finite indices and truncations only; the all-site and boundary asymptotic proof uses the resolvent and analytic maximization.
